newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power steady amid firmer Fla demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power steady amid firmer Fla demand.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. were steady Monday versus Friday's values amid keen buying interest, firmer demand in Florida and still tight generating capacity, market sources said.
"Florida is coming back up," said one Southeast trader, referring to emerging heating demand in parts of the state during off-peak hours.
Temperatures in Florida were forecast to peak in the 70s to 80s Fahrenheit. and to bottom in the 40s to 50s on Tuesday.
According to the Weather Service Corp, weather in the Southeast will be on a slow moderating trend to near or even slightly warmer than normal as the week progresses.
The Southern Co was heard to be an active player, both as buyer and seller, in today's market.

Generating capacity was still somewhat reduced with the outage of Carolina Power & Light Co's 683 megawatt (MW) Robinson nuclear power unit 2 in Hartsville, S.C. and Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) 1,148 MW Sequoyah 2 in Soddy-Daisy, Tenn.
The Robinson facility was running at low power today, and expected to resume full output by the end of the week. Sequoyah 2 was still off line until its scheduled startup Thursday.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Tuesday was quoted at $21.00-$23.50 a megawatt hour, a wider range than Friday's $22.00-$23.00 for Monday delivery.
Firm, off-peak electricity for next-day delivery was valued at $15.00-$16.00, flat from Friday's quote.
Up in the northern portion of TVA system, firm, peak electricity was assessed at $17.00-$18.00, unchanged from Friday's range.
Off-peak, firm power in northern TVA for Tuesday delivery was mostly pegged near $12.00, flat from Friday.
